chunks: And what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Sayf ibn ʿAmīrah, from Bakr ibn Abī Bakr al-Ḥaḍramī, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: Does a man sleep while he is sitting? He said: My father used to say: When a man sleeps while sitting, gathered together, then there is no wudu (ablution) upon him; but when he sleeps lying down, then wudu (ablution) is upon him.

And whatever proceeds along the lines of these two reports among what has been transmitted, containing the negation of repeating wudu (ablution) due to sleep, is abundant; we did not mention it because the discussion concerning it is one and the same: that we carry it upon sleep which does not overcome the intellect, and with which the person remains composed and aware of what proceeds from him.

And that which indicates this interpretation is what al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me of, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ṣaffār, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā and al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān together, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl, from Abī al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Kinānī, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who dozes while he is in salat (prayer). He said: If he does not retain awareness of any hadath issuing from him, then wudu (ablution) and repeating the salat (prayer) are upon him. But if he is certain that no hadath occurred, then there is no wudu (ablution) upon him, nor any repetition.

key_terms.إِعَادَةُ: repetition, here referring to repeating the salat (prayer)
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the ritual prayer during which the dozing person is being discussed
key_terms.النَّوْمِ: sleep, discussed here as affecting ritual purity depending on its depth
key_terms.الْعَقْلِ: awareness or intellect, indicating retained consciousness during sleep
key_terms.حَدَثًا: a state-breaking occurrence that nullifies ritual purity
key_terms.مُضْطَجِعًا: lying down, a posture associated here with requiring wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: Does sleeping while sitting invalidate wudu (ablution) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling of sleep in relation to wudu (ablution), distinguishing between light sleep while sitting and deeper sleep while lying down or losing awareness. It also clarifies that the decisive factor is whether sleep overcomes awareness such that a person can no longer know if hadath occurred, especially during salat (prayer).
